punchline: On Hans Rosling's basic questions about the world, a chimpanzee picking at random would beat most educated audiences.
thirty_sec: Hans Rosling asked thousands of people, including experts and leaders, simple three-option questions. What share of the world's one-year-olds are vaccinated? Has extreme poverty halved, doubled, or stayed the same? Random guessing gets about a third right. Most groups did worse. And their mistakes weren't random: people kept picking the gloomiest answer. Rosling's conclusion was that the problem isn't missing knowledge but an overdramatic view of the world.
question: Is there something you were sure was getting worse in the world, and then found out wasn't?
